narration.text: That pop when you crack your knuckles?
Nothing is grinding, and nothing is snapping.
Each knuckle is a joint sealed inside a capsule of slippery fluid.
When you pull or bend it, the joint surfaces separate, and the pressure inside drops fast.
Gas dissolved in that fluid suddenly forms a bubble. That’s the pop.
In 2015, researchers watched it happen in real time inside an MRI scanner.
You can’t crack the same knuckle again right away. The reset takes about twenty minutes.
Does it cause arthritis? One doctor cracked only one hand for sixty years. Neither hand got arthritis. One person—not proof.
So crack away. Follow for what’s really happening inside you.
